§12.1.2 Images and Figures

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

images-images-and-figures · rule diagrams images

✅ Normative

The output MUST NOT contain an image reference ![caption](path) or a bracketed placeholder such as [The image shows…]. A figure's content MUST be rendered as text, a table or a diagram — whichever the figure actually is.

An output is consumed by a model or an extraction step. An image reference is a dead end to both; the content has to be in the text stream.

Choosing the form

The figure is really… Rendering
A data display (chart, plot) A chart table — Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1
A graph of relationships A diagram/<language> fenced block (for example diagram/mermaid or diagram/plantUml) — Diagrams and Flowcharts§12.2.2
A labelled schematic A suitable diagram/<language> block; description only if none can preserve it — Slide Diagrams§12.2.5
A photo or decorative art A prose description of what it shows
Text rendered as an image The text, transcribed

Equations

Equations MUST be LaTeX in $$ … $$, inline ones included — see Inline Equations§7.2.6. Using $$ uniformly keeps a stray currency symbol elsewhere on the page from opening an unterminated math span.

Multi-column pages

Multi-column text MUST be unrolled into a single column in reading order. The physical column split is a typesetting artefact, not structure, and MUST NOT be preserved — see Reading Order§5.9.
